elements.element: Restriction limited to a named competing product/scope
elements.evidence: "shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products, and HDI" — open-ended "products substantially similar ... Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar" removed

elements.element: Restriction operates during the term only
elements.evidence: "during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate"; no post-term tail survives
Only "during the term of this Agreement" appears; no 12-month outside limit on the restriction is stated anywhere in the redlined clause
"(ii) internally developing web sites or e-commerce capabilities"
"(iii) continuing to operate any business or web site acquired by, or merged with, the Company or any of its affiliates"

elements.element: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer at all
elements.evidence: "the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products" remains, plus HDI "exclusive right to use of the 'Deerskin' brand"

Nothing in this Section 6.1 shall restrict the Company from
reasons: Fallback is incomplete: the redline narrows scope and adds the internal-development and acquisition carve-outs but never caps the restriction's duration at 12 months; it runs for the whole (indefinite) term of the Agreement. Add a short cap such as 'and in any event for no longer than twelve (12) months'.
Preferred position is not met and was not targeted: a field-of-use restriction on the Company plus HDI's exclusivity remain in force.

Minimality fails. Operation 2 replaces a 13-word anchor with 66 words (official gate: ratio 5.08 > 1.50) and operation 1's changed-character ratio 0.886 exceeds the 0.600 limit; a tighter deletion plus a single short carve-out sentence would suffice.

Carve-out (i) ('any products other than Deerskin Products through any channel') is surplus duplicated protection — the narrowed scope already reaches only Deerskin Products — and 'merged with' / 'any of its affiliates' broaden the acquisition carve-out beyond what the fallback requires.
Intent is preserved: HDI's exclusive 'Deerskin' brand right, the term limitation, and Section 6.2's closeout carve-out remain effective, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
